note:
10 pages total (9 content pages + home), organised under a 6-item main nav — Home, About, Programs, Impact, Our Jamii, Contact — per the client's explicit page list. This is a deliberate IA consolidation from the original 21-page inventory (see docs/content-seeding-plan.md §2 for the historical breakdown), carried out to remove duplicate hero headers, duplicate CTA bands and a 5-group dropdown mega-nav that fragmented closely related content across too many thin pages. 'about' absorbed the former 'problem' and 'careers' pages as in-page subsections; 'programs' absorbed 'results', 'register', 'requirements', 'calendar' and 'findus'; 'partnerships' absorbed 'partner', 'government', 'finance', 'donors' and 'corporate'; 'impact' absorbed 'stories' and 'reports'; 'form' was renamed to 'apply' unchanged in substance. 'news-events' was split back out of 'impact' on a follow-up request — it absorbed the former 'latest' and 'events' pages, which had briefly lived as anchored sections on 'impact' during the first consolidation pass. 'partnerships', 'apply' and 'news-events' are three of the pages judged too distinct to fold further into their parent as plain sections — partnerships is a five-audience institutional-relations page, apply is a transactional multi-step form, and news-events is fast-changing/dated content that would otherwise sit awkwardly next to impact's mostly-static annual narrative — each is kept as its own page, reached only via a submenu (see ../navigation.json: About > Partnerships, Programs > Register / Apply, Impact > News & events) and via in-page CTAs, not as flat top-level nav items. 'slug' is this plan's recommended real WordPress permalink slug, replacing the template's '#/<key>' hash route — see content-seeding-plan.md decision #2. 'key' is stable and matches the filename in pages/<key>.json and the template's original route id, so it survives if the slug is renamed later.

'jamii' added 2026-08-21 — not part of the original 21-page inventory or the consolidation above, so it isn't covered by any of the absorption history described here. It introduces Esoqo's Our Jamii product (the free per-group public page + fundraising campaigns every CECF-registered group gets) and is a real top-level nav item on its own, not a submenu child, since it's a distinct product rather than more CECF program copy. Its CTAs resolve externally via App\Support\PageUrl::esoqoJamiiUrl(), not to another local page — see pages/jamii.json.

'team' (staff/board, reached via About's submenu) and 'who-we-serve' (the categories of community CECF works with — MSMEs, women's groups, youth, gender/GBV support, vulnerable communities, refugees, persons with disabilities, older persons — also via About's submenu) came from the wordpress branch's block-editor/Customizer pass and were merged back into this history afterwards. 'who-we-serve' was originally drafted as its own top-level page keyed 'our-jamii', sharing both the 'our-jamii' slug and the 'Our Jamii' framing with the unrelated Esoqo-product page above; renamed on merge to avoid the collision — it is about the communities CECF serves, not the Esoqo Our Jamii product, and stays a submenu page rather than a flat top-level item like 'jamii' does. 'team' and 'who-we-serve' round out 'partnerships', 'apply' and 'news-events' as pages too distinct to fold into their parent as a section (team is a people list; who-we-serve is an audience taxonomy).
